questions.text: How is a "project" defined in the material?
options: A temporary endeavor with a unique goal and usually a budget
A permanent business function with recurring output
An informal team activity with no defined goal
A single-person task with unlimited time
questions.explanation: A project is defined as a temporary endeavor that has a unique goal and usually a budget.

questions.text: Project management is the application of processes, methods, skills, knowledge, and experience to achieve project objectives within which agreed-upon parameters?
questions.explanation: Project management aims to deliver a result within agreed-upon scope, time, cost, and quality parameters.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as reasons project management is important?
questions.explanation: The material lists Organization and Structure, Improved Efficiency, Stakeholder Satisfaction, Risk Management, and Achieving Strategic Goals. Guaranteed profit is not one of them.

questions.text: Match each project management importance area to its description.
allChoices: Brings structure to processes that could otherwise be chaotic
Resources are allocated optimally, leading to higher productivity and cost savings
Ensures clear communication with stakeholders, keeping them informed and engaged
Enables teams to identify, assess, and mitigate risks
Projects are essential vehicles to drive organizational change and meet strategic objectives

pairs.match: Brings structure to processes that could otherwise be chaotic
Resources are allocated optimally, leading to higher productivity and cost savings
Ensures clear communication with stakeholders, keeping them informed and engaged
Enables teams to identify, assess, and mitigate risks
Projects are essential vehicles to drive organizational change and meet strategic objectives

questions.explanation: Each importance area maps to a distinct benefit described under "Importance of Project Management."

questions.text: Which role of the Project Manager involves developing a comprehensive project plan that outlines the scope, schedule, resources, and budget?
questions.explanation: Planning covers developing the comprehensive project plan (scope, schedule, resources, budget).

questions.text: Which PM role involves leading the project team and coordinating activities to ensure timely delivery?
questions.explanation: Execution covers leading the team and coordinating activities for timely delivery.

questions.text: Which PM role focuses on identifying and managing potential risks to minimize their impact on the project?
questions.explanation: Risk Management covers identifying and managing potential risks.

questions.text: Which PM role involves addressing challenges and conflicts that arise during the project lifecycle?
questions.explanation: Problem-Solving covers addressing challenges and conflicts during the lifecycle.

questions.text: Which PM role keeps stakeholders updated on progress, issues, and changes through regular communication?
questions.explanation: Communication covers keeping stakeholders updated on progress, issues, and changes.

questions.text: Project Performance Domains are a group of related activities that are critical for the effective delivery of project ___.
questions.explanation: Performance Domains are described as critical for the effective delivery of project outcomes.

questions.text: Which of the following are among the 8 Project Performance Domains listed in the material?
questions.explanation: The 8 domains listed are Team, Stakeholders, Development Approach and Life Cycle, Planning, Project Work, Delivery, Measurement, and Uncertainty. "Budgeting" is not named as its own domain.

questions.text: How is a "Stakeholder" defined in the material?
options: An individual, group, or organization that may affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a decision, activity, or outcome of a project
Only the paying client of a project
Any employee within the performing organization
questions.explanation: This is the definition given for a stakeholder.

questions.text: How is "Stakeholder Analysis" defined?
options: A method of systematically gathering and analyzing quantitative and qualitative information to determine whose interests should be taken into account throughout the project
A financial audit of stakeholder contracts
A survey sent only at project closure
A ranking of stakeholders by job title
questions.explanation: This is the definition given for Stakeholder Analysis.

questions.text: Which stakeholder management tool maps stakeholders by power and interest to enhance project management efficiency and foster better relationships?
questions.explanation: The Power-Interest Matrix is listed as enhancing project management efficiency and fostering better stakeholder relationships.

questions.text: Which document is described as used throughout the project, closely related to the communication plan, to manage stakeholder interactions?
questions.explanation: The Stakeholder Register is used throughout the project and is closely related to the project communication plan.

questions.text: Who is described as signing off that the project is complete, and is "the one the PM has to satisfy"?
questions.explanation: The Project Sponsor signs off that the project is complete.

questions.text: The Project Sponsor is usually inside the project team.
questions.explanation: The material states the sponsor "may be inside but is usually outside the project."

questions.text: What does RTM stand for in project management?
questions.explanation: RTM stands for Requirements Traceability Matrix.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as typical columns/fields of a Requirements Traceability Matrix?
questions.explanation: RTM columns include Requirement ID, Requirement Description, Source, Related Test Cases, Design and Implementation Details, Verification Status, and Priority. Employee Salary is not one of them.

questions.text: Match each type of RTM traceability to its description.
allChoices: Tracks requirements from inception to ensure they are covered by design, development, and test cases
Ensures every element in the final product can be traced back to its original requirement
A combination of forward and backward traceability

pairs.match: Tracks requirements from inception to ensure they are covered by design, development, and test cases
Ensures every element in the final product can be traced back to its original requirement
A combination of forward and backward traceability

questions.explanation: Forward traceability goes requirement-to-test, backward goes final-product-to-requirement, and bi-directional combines both.

questions.text: Which RTM benefit involves linking requirements to test cases to identify and fix gaps early in the development process?
questions.explanation: Defect Prevention is achieved by linking requirements to test cases to catch gaps early.

questions.text: Which RTM tool is described as "widely used due to its simplicity and flexibility"?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Excel is described as widely used for RTMs due to its simplicity and flexibility.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as challenges of maintaining an RTM?
questions.explanation: The listed challenges are Complexity, Frequent Updates, and Manual Errors. Automation is instead listed as a best practice, not a challenge.

questions.text: One RTM best practice states: "___ early: Create the RTM at the beginning of the project and update it continuously."
questions.explanation: The best practice is "Start early: Create the RTM at the beginning of the project and update it continuously."

questions.text: In the RTM class exercise, what kind of system are students tasked with tracking requirements for?
options: An online learning platform for a university
questions.explanation: The exercise scenario is developing an online learning platform for a university.

questions.text: In the RTM exercise, the Requirement Type column classifies each requirement as Functional (F) or Non-Functional (NF).
questions.explanation: The RTM template's Requirement Type column classifies requirements as Functional (F) or Non-Functional (NF).
